messages.author: d366568c6440609c
messages.subject: compiling sparse matrices (S4 object error)
parts:
Hi!

I am trying to use a sparse design matrix in my model, created using the Matrix package. Its class is "dgCMatrix", and it's an S4 object. I'm encountering issues when I attempt to compile the model and mcmc object, getting the below error message:

"Error in storage.mode(values) <- "numeric" : no method for coercing this S4 class to a vector"

Is there a different way to implement sparse matrices in nimble, that will allow for compilation? Or is there a step I should take to coerce the sparse matrix into a different class before compiling? 

Thank you in advance for your help!

best,
Liz

messages.author: dd632bd3bbcdd7e9
messages.subject: Re: compiling sparse matrices (S4 object error)
parts:
Currently there is no sparse matrix support built into nimble.  It is on our long-term agenda.

Variables (and nodes) in models must be basic numeric types: vectors, matrices, arrays.  One way you might be able to do it is if there is a way to convert from dgCMatrix to a vector and back.  If you can share more about the use case, we might be able to come up with ideas.

-Perry

Hi Perry,

Thanks for the swift reply - I appreciate your help with this!

I'm working with a design matrix of dimension 33180 x 3472. This matrix captures 3 ecoregion levels I'm working with, so I have 112 dummy variable columns for ecoregion. I then have 30 columns of univariate basis vectors for the covariates I'm interested in. The remaining columns are interaction effects between each ecoregion column and basis vector. 97% of the elements in this matrix are zero entries, which is why I was hoping to use a sparse design matrix in my model. 

Not sure if this is relevant/helpful in coming up with a solution, but the model I'm using this matrix in is below: 
ZIPcode_icar <- nimbleCode({
  # params for mu and pi calculations  
  # i = 2 -> one for mu and one for pi
  for(i in 1:2) {
    alpha[i] ~ dnorm(0,5) # scalar intercept params
    eta[i] ~ dbeta(8,2) # AR param for spatio-temporal adjustments
    sigma_phi[i] ~ dnorm(0,1)  # time difference spatial sd
    beta_param[i] ~ dunif(0,1) # AR param for betas 
    tau[i] ~ dnorm(0,5) # precision param
  }
  
  # AR(1) on betas - for overfitting
  beta_sd <- 0.01
  for(i in 1:2) {
    beta[i,1] ~ dnorm(0, sd = sqrt(beta_sd))    
    for(k in 2:p) {
      beta[i,k] ~ dnorm(beta_param[i] * beta[i, k-1], sd = sqrt(beta_sd)) 
    }
  }
  
  # spatio-temporal effects
  # IAR prior (spatial)
  for(i in 1:2) {
    phi_sp[1:s, 1, i] ~ dcar_normal(adj = adj[1:L], weights = weights[1:L], num = num[1:s], tau = tau[i])
  }

  # temporal
  for(i in 1:2) {
    phi_full[1:s,1,i] <- phi_sp[1:s, 1, i] * sigma_phi[i]
    for(m in 2:t) {
      phi_full[1:s,m,i] <- eta[i] * phi_full[1:s, m-1, i]  + phi_sp[1:s, 1, i] * sigma_phi[i]
    }
  }
  
  #likelihood
  for(m in 1:t) {
    for(j in 1:s) {
      log(u[j,m]) <- alpha[1] + inprod(beta[1, 1:p], x[j, 1:p]) + phi_full[j, m, 1] + log_area[j]
      logit(pi_param[j,m]) <- alpha[2] + inprod(beta[2, 1:p], x[j, 1:p]) + phi_full[j,m, 2]
    }
  }
  
  # vectorize mu and pi
  mu[1:(s*t)] <- nimC(u[1:s,1:t])
  pi[1:(s*t)] <- nimC(pi_param[1:s,1:t])
  
  for(q in 1:(s*t)) {
    y[q] ~ dZIP(mu[q], zeroProb = pi[q])
  }
})

best,
Liz

messages.author: c9e9cbbfb3b043f0
messages.subject: Re: compiling sparse matrices (S4 object error)
parts:
Liz, thanks for your interest in nimble.

I've had some success using sparse matrix functions from the Matrix package in nimble.  Specifically, by calling out to Matrix package functions using nimbleRcall.  I maintained the content of the sparse matrices in {row index, column index, value} format, then called out to specifiec sparse matrix functions from the Matrix package.  It took a little bit of setup, but worked in the end.  You can see examples of this in action in the BayesNSGP package, in the fole SGV.R, specifically functions such as R_sparse_tcrossprod, nimble_sparse_tcrossprod, etc:
https://github.com/danielturek/BayesNSGP/blob/master/BayesNSGP/R/SGV.R

These examples might help get you started.

Cheers,
Daniel

https://github.com/danielturek/BayesNSGP/blob/master/BayesNSGP/R/SGV.R

These examples might help get you started.

Cheers,
Daniel

ZIPcode_icar <- nimbleCode({
  # params for mu and pi calculations  
  # i = 2 -> one for mu and one for pi
  for(i in 1:2) {

    eta[i] ~ dbeta(8,2) # AR param for spatio-temporal adjustments
    sigma_phi[i] ~ dnorm(0,1)  # time difference spatial sd
    beta_param[i] ~ dunif(0,1) # AR param for betas 
    tau[i] ~ dnorm(0,5) # precision param
  }
  
  # AR(1) on betas - for overfitting

  for(i in 1:2) {
    beta[i,1] ~ dnorm(0, sd = sqrt(beta_sd))

    }
  }
  
  # spatio-temporal effects

    }

  }

}

## source: Perry and Daniel from nimble_users

## Define the nimbleRcall nimbleFunctions to call the R function
RcalcXB_model <- nimbleRcall(function(beta = double(1)) {}, returnType = double(1), Rfun = 'RcalcXB_int')

ZIPcode_icar <- nimbleCode({
  # params for mu and pi calculations  
  # i = 2 -> one for mu and one for pi
  for(i in 1:2) {
    alpha[i] ~ dnorm(0,5) # scalar intercept params

    sigma_phi[i] ~ dnorm(0,1)  # time difference spatial sd
    beta_param[i] ~ dunif(0,1) # AR param for betas

    }
  }
  
  # spatio-temporal effects

  for(i in 1:2) {
    phi_sp[1:s, 1, i] ~ dcar_normal(adj = adj[1:L], weights = weights[1:L], num = num[1:s], tau = tau[i])
  }

  # temporal
  for(i in 1:2) {
    phi_full[1:s,1,i] <- phi_sp[1:s, 1, i] * sigma_phi[i]
    for(m in 2:t) {
      phi_full[1:s,m,i] <- eta[i] * phi_full[1:s, m-1, i]  + phi_sp[1:s, 1, i] * sigma_phi[i]
    }
  }

#likelihood params and calculations
  XB[1:(s*t),1] <- RcalcXB_model(beta[1, 1:p])
  XB[1:(s*t),2] <- RcalcXB_model(beta[2, 1:p])

for(m in 1:t) {
    for(j in 1:s) {

log(u[j,m]) <- alpha[1] + XB[((m-1) * s + j),1] + phi_full[j, m, 1] + log_area[j]
        logit(pi_param[j,m]) <- alpha[2] + XB[((m-1) * s + j),2] + phi_full[j,m, 2]

}
  }
  
  # vectorize mu and pi

  for(q in 1:(s*t)) {
    y[q] ~ dZIP(mu[q], zeroProb = pi[q])
  }
})

Currently there is no sparse matrix support built into nimble.  It is on our long-term agenda.

Variables (and nodes) in models must be basic numeric types: vectors, matrices, arrays.  One way you might be able to do it is if there is a way to convert from dgCMatrix to a vector and back.  If you can share more about the use case, we might be able to come up with ideas.

-Perry
  

On Fri, Jul 17, 2020 at 6:03 PM Liz Lawler <esla...@gmail.com> wrote:
Hi!

I am trying to use a sparse design matrix in my model, created using the Matrix package. Its class is "dgCMatrix", and it's an S4 object. I'm encountering issues when I attempt to compile the model and mcmc object, getting the below error message:

"Error in storage.mode(values) <- "numeric" : no method for coercing this S4 class to a vector"

Is there a different way to implement sparse matrices in nimble, that will allow for compilation? Or is there a step I should take to coerce the sparse matrix into a different class before compiling?
